Route / precedent: Chloride electrolysis; operating overseas and historical U.S. precedent
Feed entering extraction: Purified, suitably dehydrated chloride; not untreated brine
U.S. development opportunity — analysis: Adapt established metal extraction to a competitive domestic feed-preparation and power system.
What remains to prove: Integrated feed cost, chlorine use or disposition, sustained recovery and availability. Magrathea’s pilot evidence is separate from commercial supply.

Feed entering extraction: Prepared MgO in a molten fluoride electrolyte in the documented research
U.S. development opportunity — analysis: Investigate a route that bypasses making a dry chloride feed.
What remains to prove: Electrolyte management, oxygen-producing anode durability and magnesium collection at scale. The project later emphasized Mg–Nd master alloy, a different product.

Feed entering extraction: DOE describes dolomite plus aluminum scrap; purchased MgO is separately proposed
U.S. development opportunity — analysis: Benchmark another domestic route against the electrochemical options.
What remains to prove: Continuous-run demonstration, final feed mix, product sales and commercial cost. Aluminum is a chemical reductant: this is not electrolysis.
